newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares rose again on Thursday, with the main AEX index setting another record-high close, adding 3.57 points to end at 820.69 after having touched 822.69 during the session.

Trade started rather quietly but picked up later on in the session as market players threw their weight behind newcomer Vedior, which started trading at 1030 GMT and topped the volume list at the end of the day.
Shares in the employment services group began trading on the Amsterdam bourse at 48.00 guilders, by far outstripping the issue price of 39.00 guilders.
Dealers said market sentiment toward Vedior was positive, but added the stock did not merit the same valuation as Dutch sector leader, Randstad.
"Vedior and Randstad can't be compared. Randstad has a very solid market position in the Netherlands, and it has proven itself much more than Vedior," Fernand de Boer, analyst at SNS Securities said.
Dealers said they expected Vedior shares to maintain their current run initially, adding the real market valuation of the stock would only appear in a matter of weeks.
"Once the lead managers take their hands off them, we'll see what the market really thinks of Vedior," one dealer said.
Randstad shed 3.30 guilders to close at 200.20, while Vendex ended down 2.60 guilders at 113.10. Dealers said some market players were switching out of these two and into Vedior.
The high techs performed well. ASM Lithograpy climbed 0.50 guilders to 97.50. BE Semiconductor added 0.60 to 28.40.
Philips continued its way up with dealers saying a major bank mentioned a share price goal of 150 guilders for the stock. The share gained 1.40 guilders to close at 119.30.

KPN continued to benefit from yesterday's announcement the Unisource partnership would lead to major cost savings. Fuelled also by speculation of a possible split of the company into telecom and a postal units, and broker upgrades, the shares rose 0.40 guilders to 75.00.
The chemical sector also did well. Akzo ended 4.80 guilders higher at 258.00 and DSM climbed 3.50 to 191.80 guilders.
Dealers said a bullish presentation held in London boosted the shares.
